n: A guilty conscience makes the wicked run even when no one is chasing them; the righteous are bold as lions.

f.w: The wicked flee when no man pursueth

n: When a nation rebels, rulers come and go quickly; a wise, discerning leader brings lasting stability. Northern Israel’s many short-lived kings illustrate this.
A poor person who oppresses other poor people is like a driving rain that washes away crops instead of watering them.

f.w: a sweeping rain which leaveth no food
f.g: A torrential storm that flattens and destroys crops.

n: Abandoning God’s law leads people to praise the wicked; keeping it leads people to oppose them.
Evil people don’t understand justice, but those who seek the Lord understand it fully. Spiritual understanding comes from seeking God.

f.w: they that seek the LORD understand all things

n: Better to be poor and live with integrity than to be rich and crooked.

f.w: Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness

n: A child who keeps God’s law is wise; one who hangs out with gluttons shames his father.
Wealth gained by charging the poor excessive interest will end up with someone who is kind to the poor.

f.g: usury = interest; Israel’s law forbade charging interest to a poor fellow Israelite.

n: If someone refuses to listen to God’s law, even their prayers are detestable. God hears those who are willing to hear him.

f.w: even his prayer shall be abomination

n: Whoever leads the upright astray will fall into his own trap, but the blameless will inherit good things.

f.w: causeth the righteous to go astray

n: The rich may think themselves wise, but a poor person with insight can see right through them.
When the righteous triumph, there is great celebration; when the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding.
Hiding sins leads nowhere good, but confessing and abandoning them brings mercy. A key verse on repentance.

f.w: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper

n: Blessed is the one who always reveres God, but whoever hardens their heart falls into trouble.

f.g: Always stays reverent and careful before God.

n: A wicked ruler over poor people is like a roaring lion or a charging bear.
A ruler without understanding is a cruel oppressor; one who hates dishonest gain will reign a long time.
A murderer, tormented by guilt, is a fugitive until death; let no one help him escape.

f.g: Let no one hold him back or support him.

n: Whoever walks with integrity will be kept safe; whoever is crooked will suddenly fall.

f.w: Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved

n: Working your land brings plenty of food; chasing fantasies brings plenty of poverty. (Nearly repeats 12:11.)
A faithful person will be richly blessed, but one eager to get rich quick won’t stay innocent.

f.w: he that maketh haste to be rich

n: Showing favoritism is wrong—yet some will do wrong for just a piece of bread. Partiality can be bought cheaply.
The stingy hurry to get rich, not realizing poverty is coming.
Whoever corrects someone will in the end gain more favor than one who flatters.

f.w: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour

n: Whoever robs his own parents and says, “It’s not wrong,” is no better than a vandal.

f.w: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother

n: A greedy, arrogant person stirs up conflict; whoever trusts the Lord will prosper.
Trusting only your own mind is foolish; walking in wisdom keeps you safe.

f.w: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool

n: Whoever gives to the poor will lack nothing, but whoever looks away from them will receive many curses.

f.w: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack

f.g: Looks away from need on purpose.

n: When the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding; when they perish, the righteous flourish.
